title: Jude and the Wreck
premise: Coral Galloway has spent a decade mapping the closed rail lines of the northern wilderness, keeping his past buried as deep as his survey stakes. When a government expedition vanishes near an abandoned junction, he is the only man who knows the terrain well enough to find them—and the only one who recognizes what their gear was really looking for. Leading the rescue means guiding people whose mission threatens to expose both the line's buried history and Coral's own hidden identity. In the end, Coral brings the survivors home but chooses loyalty to the dead over the truth the government wants, burning the final map and letting the wilderness keep its secret.
about_author: Juniper Voss is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six seasons working remote rail corridors before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and protagonists who would rather disappear than explain themselves.

chapters.title: The Last Spike Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishing chapter: Coral works the dying rail lines alone, trading maps for supplies in a town that asks no questions. A telegram arrives requesting his services for a search. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the life he built on anonymity is about to be tested.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He reaches the expedition's last camp: tents intact, instruments running, food untouched, and not a single footprint leaving it. The official story doesn't fit what he sees. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into suspicion—someone erased these people deliberately.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Were For
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a flashback to his old crew. Examining the abandoned equipment, he realizes the team wasn't surveying terrain—they were searching for something sealed inside the old tunnel at Wreck Junction, the site of the disaster that ended his first career. Emotional beat: recognition and fear of being recognized himself.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signed the Telegram
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Ilsa Brandt, the expedition's deputy who stayed behind, now insisting on joining Coral's search. She's sharp, watchful, and clearly knows more about the mission than her file admits. Emotional beat: wary alliance—two people each hiding something, using each other.

chapters.title: Dry Season Countdown
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilsa push upriver as water levels drop, cutting off their return route day by day. They find the first survivor—half-dead, raving about lights under the mountain. Emotional beat: urgency compounding; the wilderness is closing its doors behind them.

chapters.title: Wreck Junction
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the sealed tunnel and discover the missing surveyors alive but barricaded inside, guarding what they found: records proving the original disaster was covered up—a collapse caused by orders, not geology, with Coral's old crew named as scapegoats. Emotional beat: the past breaking open like a fault line.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She reveals she was sent to verify the cover-up and offers Coral vindication if he testifies—but testimony means exposing the survivors' discovery and dragging every family involved back into the light. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as temptation; Coral must weigh truth against mercy.

chapters.title: The River Takes Its Toll
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Racing the dry season home, they lose their boats and gear crossing a flash flood; one surveyor drowns saving another. The group fractures over whether Ilsa should be allowed to report anything at all. Emotional beat: grief and hardening resolve—Coral becomes the leader he never wanted to be.

chapters.title: Testimony at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Climax. A second government party intercepts them at the last passable ford, demanding the records. Coral stalls them with a false route through collapsing badlands while the survivors slip across the river. Emotional beat: Coral finally acts openly, spending his invisibility like currency to buy others' safety.

chapters.title: What the Wilderness Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue-adjacent. Home again, Coral gives the inquiry everything except the final map, which he burns—letting the dead keep their names clean and the mountain keep its secret. Ilsa leaves without reporting him. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; identity chosen, memory honored, truth rationed like water.
